data_objects.name: respondent_wage_characteristics
data_objects.meaning: Individual-level wage records with experience, education, appearance rating, health, demographic, geographic, union, marital, and occupation indicators.
data_objects.notes: No respondent identifier, survey context, reference period, or measurement-unit metadata is supplied.

variables.name: wage
variables.meaning: Reported wage value for the individual; the currency and pay period are not declared.

variables.name: belavg
variables.meaning: Binary below-average-appearance indicator: 1 for looks codes below the middle code and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: abvavg
variables.meaning: Binary above-average-appearance indicator: 1 for looks codes above the middle code and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: looks
variables.meaning: Ordinal appearance-rating code whose middle code is treated as average by the related indicators.

variables.name: union
variables.meaning: Binary union-membership indicator, encoded 1 for membership and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: goodhlth
variables.meaning: Binary indicator named for good health, encoded 1 when the named condition applies and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: black
variables.meaning: Binary racial-category indicator named Black, encoded 1 for that category and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: female
variables.meaning: Binary sex or gender category indicator named female, encoded 1 for that category and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: married
variables.meaning: Binary marital-status indicator, encoded 1 for married and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: south
variables.meaning: Binary geographic indicator named South, encoded 1 when the named region applies and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: bigcity
variables.meaning: Binary residence indicator named big city, encoded 1 when that category applies and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: smllcity
variables.meaning: Binary residence indicator named small city, encoded 1 when that category applies and 0 otherwise.

variables.name: service
variables.meaning: Binary service-occupation indicator, encoded 1 for service and 0 for non-service.

variables.name: Nservice
variables.meaning: Binary non-service-occupation indicator, encoded as the complement of service.

variables.name: Slooks
variables.meaning: Service-gated appearance value: it equals looks for service records and zero for non-service records.

structure.description: Each row represents one individual record. No source column is an explicit row identifier, and row order has no declared semantic meaning.
lwage is a logarithmic counterpart of wage, and expersq is a squared counterpart of exper.
belavg and abvavg partition non-middle looks ratings below and above the middle category; Nservice complements service, and Slooks combines service status with looks.

uncertainties: The currency and pay period of wage, and the units of exper and educ, are not declared.
The survey population, sampling frame, reference period, and exact questionnaire definitions are absent.
The binary field names support their positive-category interpretations, but no separate codebook defines the underlying demographic, geographic, health, or occupation categories.
annotation_notes: Semantics are grounded only in the declared train.csv evidence.
